sentences.zh: 職官誌

translations.literal: Treatise on Official Posts
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Official Posts

sentences.zh: 夫官非位無以分貴賤，位非品無以定高卑，是以歷代史官，咸有所紀，皆窮源而討本，期與世以作程。

translations.literal: For if offices had no ranks, there would be no way to distinguish noble from base; if ranks had no grades, there would be no way to fix high and low. Therefore historians of every dynasty all recorded such matters, tracing each to its source and examining its root, hoping to set a standard for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Without ranks, offices could not distinguish noble from common; without grades, ranks could not fix precedence high and low. That is why historians of every era recorded these matters, tracing each institution to its origin, so that their age might have a standard to follow.

sentences.zh: 迨乎唐祚方隆，玄宗在宥，采累朝之故事，考眾職之遐源，申命才臣，著成《六典》，其勛階之等級，品秩之重輕，則已備載於其中矣。

translations.literal: When the Tang fortune was flourishing and Emperor Xuanzong reigned in grace, he gathered precedents of successive dynasties, investigated the remote origins of all offices, charged talented ministers, and compiled the Administrative Regulations, whose grades of merit ranks and relative weight of titles and ranks were already fully recorded therein.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fortunes rose and Emperor Xuanzong held court, he collected precedents from successive reigns, traced the ancient origins of every office, and charged able ministers to compile the Administrative Regulations, which already set out in full the grades of merit ranks and the relative weight of titles and ranks.

sentences.zh: 故今之所撰，不敢相沿，祖述五代之命官，以踵百王之垂範，或厘革升降，則謹而誌之，俾後之為天官卿者，得以觀焉。

translations.literal: Therefore what is compiled here does not dare simply to follow that model but traces the appointment of officials under the Five Dynasties, to continue the models left by the hundred kings; where offices were reformed or ranks raised or lowered, it records them carefully, so that future Directors of the Bureau of Astronomy may view them.
translations.idiomatic: The present compilation therefore does not simply follow the Tang model but traces how the Five Dynasties appointed officials, continuing the precedents of earlier kings. Where offices were reorganized or ranks raised or lowered, those changes are recorded carefully, so that future Directors of the Bureau of Astronomy may consult them.

sentences.zh: 梁開平三年三月，詔升尚書令為正一品。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiping of Liang, third month, an edict promoted the Minister-in-Chief to the first rank, grade one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Kaiping (909), Liang issued an edict promoting the Minister-in-Chief to first rank, grade one.

sentences.zh: 按《唐六典》，尚書令正二品，是時以將授趙州王镕此官，故升之。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Administrative Regulations, the Minister-in-Chief was second rank, grade one; at this time the throne was about to grant this office to Wang Rong of Zhao Prefecture, hence it was promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Administrative Regulations the Minister-in-Chief was second rank, grade one; because Wang Rong of Zhao was about to receive the post, the rank was raised.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成四年八月，詔曰：「朝廷每有將相恩命，準往例，諸道節度使帶平章事、兼侍中、中書令，並列銜於敕牒後，側書『使』字。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng of Later Tang, eighth month, an edict said: Whenever the court issues a gracious appointment to a general or minister, according to former precedent, military commissioners of the circuits who bear Grand Councilor, concurrent Palace Attendant, or Director of the Secretariat all have their titles listed after the edict, with the character "Commissioner" written to the side.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Tiancheng (929), Later Tang issued an edict: Whenever the court granted a favor to a general or minister, precedent required that circuit military commissioners who held Grand Councilor, concurrent Palace Attendant, or Director of the Secretariat have their titles listed after the edict, with the character "Commissioner" written beside them.

sentences.zh: 今兩浙節度使錢镠是元帥、尚父，與使相名殊，承前列銜，久未改正。

translations.literal: Now Qian Liu, military commissioner of the Two Zhes, is Grand Marshal and Esteemed Father; his titles differ from those of commissioner-ministers, yet he has long been listed in the former position without correction.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu of the Two Zhes was Grand Marshal and Esteemed Father, titles distinct from those of commissioner-ministers, yet he had long been listed in the old order without correction.

sentences.zh: 湖南節度使馬殷，先兼中書令之時，理宜齒於相位，今守太師、尚書令，是南省官資，不合列署敕尾。

translations.literal: Ma Yin, military commissioner of Hunan, when he formerly held the concurrent post of Director of the Secretariat, properly ranked with the chief ministers; now he holds Grand Preceptor and Minister-in-Chief, which are offices of the southern departments and are not appropriate to be listed at the end of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin of Hunan, when he had concurrently held Director of the Secretariat, properly ranked with the chief ministers; now he held Grand Preceptor and Minister-in-Chief, southern-department posts inappropriate for listing at the end of edicts.

sentences.zh: 今後每署將相敕牒，宜落下錢镠、馬殷官位，仍永為常式。」

translations.literal: Henceforth, whenever edicts for generals and ministers are issued, Qian Liu's and Ma Yin's titles should be omitted, and this shall forever be the regular practice."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever edicts for generals and ministers were issued, Qian Liu's and Ma Yin's titles were to be omitted, and this was to remain the standing rule."

sentences.zh: 梁開平二年四月，改左右丞為左右司侍郎，避廟諱也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping of Liang, fourth month, the Left and Right Vice Directors were changed to Left and Right Department Vice Ministers, to avoid the taboo on the imperial temple name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Kaiping (908), Liang renamed the Left and Right Vice Directors as Left and Right Department Vice Ministers, to avoid the imperial temple taboo.

sentences.zh: 至後唐同光元年十月，復舊為左右丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang of Later Tang, tenth month, the former titles of Left and Right Vice Director were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Tongguang (923), Later Tang restored the former titles of Left and Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興元年九月，詔曰：「臺轄之司，官資並設，左右貂素來相類，左右揆不至相懸，以此比方，豈宜分別。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing of Later Tang, ninth month, an edict said: In the departments under the Censorate, offices and ranks are all established; the left and right Palace Attendants have always been alike, and the left and right Vice Directors have never been far apart—in such a comparison, how can they be distinguished?
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Changxing (930), Later Tang issued an edict: In the censorial departments, offices and ranks were established together; the left and right Palace Attendants had always been comparable, and the left and right Vice Directors had never been far apart—by that analogy, how could they be treated differently?

sentences.zh: 自此宜升尚書右丞官品，與左丞並為正四品。」

translations.literal: From now on the rank of the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs should be raised, and both left and right shall be the fourth rank, grade one."
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs was to be raised to the same rank as the left, both at fourth rank, grade one."

sentences.zh: 右都省

translations.literal: — The Department of State Affairs —
translations.idiomatic: — The Department of State Affairs —

sentences.zh: 後唐長興四年九月，敕：「馮赟有經邦之茂業，宜進位於公臺，但緣平章事字犯其父名，不欲斥其家諱，可改同平章事為同中書門下二品。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Later Tang, ninth month, an edict said: Feng Yun has outstanding merit in governing the state and should be advanced to the public terrace, but because the characters "Grand Councilor" violate his father's name, and he does not wish to offend his family taboo, "Concurrent Grand Councilor" may be changed to "Concurrent Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Changxing (933), an edict said: Feng Yun had outstanding merit in governing the state and deserved advancement to the chief ministry, but because the title Grand Councilor violated his father's name and he wished to avoid his family taboo, Concurrent Grand Councilor was changed to Concurrent Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 」後至周顯德中，樞密使吳廷祚亦加同中書門下二品，避其諱也。

translations.literal: Later, in the Xiande era of Zhou, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wu Tingzuo was also given Concurrent Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, likewise to avoid his taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the Xiande era of Zhou, Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Tingzuo received the same title, likewise to avoid his taboo.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年二月，敕：「以門下侍郎、中書侍郎並為清望正三品。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, second month, an edict said: The Vice Director of the Chancellery and the Vice Director of the Secretariat shall both be esteemed clear offices of the third rank, grade one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Tianfu (940), Jin issued an edict: The Vice Directors of the Chancellery and Secretariat were both to be esteemed clear offices at third rank, grade one.

sentences.zh: 」晉天福九月，詔曰：「《六典》云：中書舍人掌侍奉進奏參議表章，凡詔旨制敕、璽書策命，皆按故事起草進畫，既下，則署而行之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Tianfu of Jin, an edict said: The Administrative Regulations state that the Secretariat Drafter manages attendance, memorial submission, consultation, and drafting of memorials and reports; all edicts, ordinances, imperial orders, sealed letters, and appointments are drafted according to precedent, submitted for imperial approval, and once issued are signed and promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianfu, Jin issued an edict: The Administrative Regulations state that the Secretariat Drafter managed attendance, memorial submission, consultation, and drafting; all edicts, ordinances, imperial orders, sealed letters, and appointments were to be drafted according to precedent, submitted for imperial approval, and once issued signed and promulgated.

sentences.zh: 其禁有四：一曰漏泄，二曰稽緩，三曰違失，四曰忘誤，所以重王命也。

translations.literal: There are four prohibitions: first, leakage; second, delay; third, error; fourth, forgetfulness and mistake—by these the royal command is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Four prohibitions applied: leakage, delay, error, and forgetfulness or mistake—by these the royal command was honored.

sentences.zh: 古昔已來，典實斯在，爰從近代，別創新名。

translations.literal: From antiquity until now the canonical practice has stood; only from recent times has a new name been created separately.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the canonical practice had stood; only in recent times had a new name been created.

sentences.zh: 今運屬興王，事從師古，俾仍舊貫，以耀前規。

translations.literal: Now that fortune belongs to a rising king, affairs should follow the ancients, so that the old practice may continue and former standards shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: Now that fortune belonged to a rising king, affairs were to follow the ancients, restoring the old practice to honor former standards.

sentences.zh: 其翰林學士院公事，宜並歸中書舍人。」

translations.literal: The official business of the Hanlin Academy should all be returned to the Secretariat Drafters."
translations.idiomatic: The official business of the Hanlin Academy was to be returned entirely to the Secretariat Drafters."

sentences.zh: 七年五月，中書門下上言：：有司檢尋長興四年八月二十一日敕：準《官品令》，侍中、中書令正三品，按《會要》，大歷二年十一月升為正二品；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted: The relevant offices searched the edict of the twenty-first day of the eighth month of the fourth year of Changxing: According to the Statutes on Official Ranks, the Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat were third rank, grade one; according to the Institutional Compendium, in the eleventh month of the second year of Dali they were raised to second rank, grade one;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year, the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: The relevant offices had searched the edict of 21 August in the fourth year of Changxing: Under the Statutes on Official Ranks, the Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat were third rank, grade one; under the Institutional Compendium, in the eleventh month of the second year of Dali (767) they had been raised to second rank, grade one;

sentences.zh: 左右常侍從三品，按《會要》，廣德二年五月升為正三品；

translations.literal: the Left and Right Regular Attendants were third rank, grade two; according to the Institutional Compendium, in the fifth month of the second year of Guangde they were raised to third rank, grade one;
translations.idiomatic: the Left and Right Regular Attendants were third rank, grade two; under the Institutional Compendium, in the fifth month of the second year of Guangde (763) they had been raised to third rank, grade one;

sentences.zh: 門下中書侍郎正四品，大歷二年十一月升為正三品；

translations.literal: the Vice Directors of the Chancellery and Secretariat were fourth rank, grade one; in the eleventh month of the second year of Dali they were raised to third rank, grade one;
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Directors of the Chancellery and Secretariat were fourth rank, grade one; in the eleventh month of the second year of Dali they had been raised to third rank, grade one;

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫正五品，按《續會要》，會昌二年十二月升為正四品，以備中書門下四品之闕；

translations.literal: the Remonstrance Grand Master was fifth rank, grade one; according to the Continued Institutional Compendium, in the twelfth month of the second year of Huichang he was raised to fourth rank, grade one, to fill the vacancy for fourth-rank posts in the Secretariat and Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: the Remonstrance Grand Master was fifth rank, grade one; under the Continued Institutional Compendium, in the twelfth month of the second year of Huichang (842) he had been raised to fourth rank, grade one, to fill the fourth-rank vacancy in the Secretariat and Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫從三品，會昌二年十二月升為正三品；

translations.literal: the Censor-in-Chief was third rank, grade two; in the twelfth month of the second year of Huichang he was raised to third rank, grade one;
translations.idiomatic: the Censor-in-Chief was third rank, grade two; in the twelfth month of the second year of Huichang he had been raised to third rank, grade one;

sentences.zh: 御史中丞正五品，亦與大夫同時升為正四品。

translations.literal: the Vice Censor-in-Chief was fifth rank, grade one; he was also raised at the same time as the Censor-in-Chief to fourth rank, grade one.
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Censor-in-Chief was fifth rank, grade one; he had been raised at the same time as the Censor-in-Chief to fourth rank, grade one.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「宜各準元敕處分，仍添入令文，永為定制。

translations.literal: An edict said: Each should be handled according to the original edict, and also added to the statute text, to be a permanent regulation forever.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: Each post was to be handled according to the original edict and added to the statute text as a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「門下侍郎，班在常侍之下，俸祿同常侍。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: The Vice Director of the Chancellery ranks below the Regular Attendant, but his salary is the same as the Regular Attendant's."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: The Vice Director of the Chancellery ranked below the Regular Attendant but received the same salary."

sentences.zh: 周顯德五年六月，敕：「諫議大夫宜依舊正五品上，仍班位在給事中之下。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, sixth month, an edict said: The Remonstrance Grand Master should remain as before at the fifth rank, grade one upper, and his court rank should still be below the Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xiande (958), Zhou issued an edict: The Remonstrance Grand Master was to remain at fifth rank, grade one upper, with court rank still below the Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 」按《唐典》，諫議大夫四員，正五品上，皆隸門下省，班在給事中之下。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Regulations, there were four Remonstrance Grand Masters, fifth rank grade one upper, all subordinate to the Chancellery, ranking below the Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Regulations there were four Remonstrance Grand Masters at fifth rank, grade one upper, all subordinate to the Chancellery and ranking below the Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 至會昌二年十一月，中書門下奏，升為正四品下，仍分為左右，以備兩省四品之闕，故其班亦升在給事中之上。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Huichang, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized to raise them to fourth rank grade one lower, and divided them into left and right, to fill the fourth-rank vacancies of the two departments; therefore their court rank was also raised above the Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Huichang (842), the Secretariat and Chancellery had memorialized to raise them to fourth rank, grade one lower, divided into left and right to fill fourth-rank vacancies in the two departments; their court rank was therefore raised above the Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 近朝自諫議大夫拜給事中者，官雖序遷，位則降等，至是以其遷次不倫，故改正焉。

translations.literal: In recent courts, when one was promoted from Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Attendant, the office advanced in sequence but the rank was lowered; now, because this promotion order was irregular, it was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: In recent courts, promotion from Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Attendant advanced the title in sequence but lowered rank; because this order was irregular, it was now corrected.

sentences.zh: ──右兩省

translations.literal: — The Two Departments —
translations.idiomatic: — The Two Departments —

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰二年十一月，制：「以前同州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事馮道為守同空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai of Later Tang, eleventh month, an appointment said: The former military commissioner of Tong Prefecture, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Councilor Feng Dao is appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Qingtai (935), an appointment named the former Tong Prefecture military commissioner, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Grand Councilor Feng Dao Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 」時議者曰：「自隋、唐以來，三公無職事，自非親王不恒置，於宰臣為加官，無單置者。

translations.literal: Commentators at the time said: Since Sui and Tang, the Three Dukes had no duties; unless one was an imperial prince they were not regularly appointed; for chief ministers they were supplementary titles, and none was appointed alone.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators at the time said: Since Sui and Tang the Three Dukes had held no duties; unless one was an imperial prince they were not regularly appointed; for chief ministers they were supplementary titles, never held alone.

sentences.zh: 」道在相位時帶司空，及罷鎮，未命官，議者不練故事，率意行之。

translations.literal: When Dao was in the chief ministry he bore Acting Minister of Works; when he left his commission he received no new appointment; commentators unversed in precedent acted on impulse.
translations.idiomatic: While in office Feng Dao had borne Acting Minister of Works; when he left his commission he received no new appointment, and commentators unversed in precedent acted on impulse.

sentences.zh: 及制出，言議紛然，或云便可綜中書書下事或云須冊拜開府。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, discussion was clamorous: some said he could at once oversee Secretariat affairs below, others that he must receive investiture and open a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was issued, debate was clamorous: some said he could at once oversee Secretariat business, others that he must receive investiture and open a bureau.

sentences.zh: 及就列，無故事，乃不就朝堂敘班，臺官兩省官入就列，方入，宰臣退，踵後先退。

translations.literal: When he took his place in court, there was no precedent; he did not enter the hall to take his rank in order. Censorate and two-department officials entered and took their places first; only then did he enter. When the chief ministers withdrew, he followed close behind and left first.
translations.idiomatic: When he took his place at court there was no precedent; he did not enter the hall to take rank in order. Censorate and two-department officials entered first; only then did he enter. When the chief ministers withdrew, he followed close behind and left first.

sentences.zh: 劉句又以罷相為僕射，出入就列，一與馮道同，議者非之。

translations.literal: Liu Xu also, having left the chief ministry for Vice Director, entered and left court in the same way as Feng Dao; commentators criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, having left the chief ministry for Vice Director, entered and left court the same way as Feng Dao; commentators criticized this.

sentences.zh: 及晉天福中，以李纮為司徒，周廣順初，以竇貞固為司徒，蘇禹珪為司空，遂以為例，議者不復有雲。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Li Hong was made Minister of Education; at the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, Dou Zhengu was made Minister of Education and Su Yugui Minister of Works; it then became precedent, and commentators no longer objected.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Li Hong was made Minister of Education; at the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, Dou Zhengu was made Minister of Education and Su Yugui Minister of Works; it then became precedent, and commentators no longer objected.

sentences.zh: ──右三公

translations.literal: — The Three Dukes —
translations.idiomatic: — The Three Dukes —

sentences.zh: 後唐天成元年夏六月，以李琪為御史大夫，自後不復除。

translations.literal: In the summer, sixth month of the first year of Tiancheng of Later Tang, Li Qi was made Censor-in-Chief; thereafter the post was never again filled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the first year of Tiancheng (926), Later Tang appointed Li Qi Censor-in-Chief; thereafter the post was never again filled.

sentences.zh: 其年冬十一月丙子，諸道進奏官上言：「今月四日，中丞上事，臣等禮合至臺，比期不越前規，依舊傳語，忽蒙處分通出，尋則再取指揮，要明審的。

translations.literal: That winter, on the day bingzi of the eleventh month, the memorial-presenting officials of the circuits submitted: On the fourth of this month, when the Vice Censor-in-Chief took office, we by ritual should have come to the Censorate. We did not exceed the former rule and, as before, requested to convey messages, but suddenly we were ordered to be admitted through. We then sought instructions again, wanting a clear ruling.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the day bingzi of the eleventh month, the circuit memorial-presenting officials submitted: On the fourth of that month, when the Vice Censor-in-Chief took office, they should by ritual have come to the Censorate. Expecting no change from precedent, they had asked to convey messages as before, but were suddenly ordered admitted through. They then sought instructions again, wanting a clear ruling.

sentences.zh: 又蒙問：大夫相公上事日如何？

translations.literal: We were also asked: On what day will the Censor-in-Chief take office?
translations.idiomatic: They were also asked: On what day would the Censor-in-Chief take office?

sentences.zh: 臣等訴云：大夫曾為宰相，進奏官伏事中書，事體之間，實為舊吏。

translations.literal: We replied: The Censor-in-Chief was formerly a chief minister; memorial-presenting officials attend upon the Secretariat—in substance we are his former subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: They replied: The Censor-in-Chief had formerly been a chief minister; memorial-presenting officials attended upon the Secretariat—in substance they were his former subordinates.

sentences.zh: 若以別官除授，合雲傳語勞來，又堅令通出。

translations.literal: If he were appointed to a different office, it would be proper to convey messages of greeting, yet we were firmly ordered to be admitted through.
translations.idiomatic: Had he been appointed to a different office, it would have been proper to convey messages of greeting, yet they were firmly ordered admitted through.

sentences.zh: 臣等出身藩府，不會朝儀，拒命則恐有奏聞，遵稟則全隳則例，伏恐此後到臺參賀，儀則不定者。

translations.literal: We come from frontier commissions and do not know court ritual; to refuse would risk a memorial to the throne, yet to obey would wholly destroy precedent—we fear that hereafter when we come to the Censorate to offer congratulations, the ritual will be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: They came from frontier commissions and did not know court ritual; to refuse risked a memorial to the throne, yet to obey would wholly destroy precedent—they feared that hereafter when they came to the Censorate to offer congratulations, the ritual would be unsettled.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「御史臺是大朝執憲之司，乃四海繩違之地，凡居中外，皆所整齊，藩侯尚展於公參，邸吏豈宜於抗禮。

translations.literal: An edict said: The Censorate is the great court's department for enforcing the law, the place where the four seas are bound for violations; all within and without are put in order by it. Even frontier lords still come to public audience—how can lodge clerks resist proper ritual?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: The Censorate was the great court's department for enforcing the law, the place where the realm was bound for violations; all within and without were put in order by it. Even frontier lords still came to public audience—how could lodge clerks resist proper ritual?

sentences.zh: 遽觀論列，可驗侮輕，但以喪亂孔多，紀綱隳紊，霜威掃地，風憲銷聲。

translations.literal: Seeing their arguments at once, one can verify their contempt and disrespect; yet because disorders were many, regulations collapsed, frostlike authority was swept away, and the wind of censure fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Their arguments at once showed contempt and disrespect; yet because disorders had been many, regulations had collapsed, censorial authority had been swept away, and the wind of censure had fallen silent.

sentences.zh: 今則景運惟新，皇圖重正，稍加提舉，漸止澆訛。

translations.literal: Now the auspicious fortune is renewed and the imperial design set right again; with slight encouragement, the flood of corruption will gradually cease.
translations.idiomatic: Now auspicious fortune was renewed and the imperial design set right again; with slight encouragement, the flood of corruption would gradually cease.

sentences.zh: 宜令御史臺，凡關舊例，並須舉行，如不稟承，當行朝典。

translations.literal: The Censorate should be ordered: wherever old precedents apply, they must all be carried out; if they are not obeyed, the court statutes shall be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate was ordered: wherever old precedents applied, they must all be carried out; if they were not obeyed, the court statutes would be enforced.

sentences.zh: 」時盧文紀初拜中丞，領事於御史府，諸道進奏官來賀，文紀曰：「事例如何？

translations.literal: At that time Lu Wenji had just been appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and was conducting affairs at the Censorate. Memorial-presenting officials of the circuits came to congratulate. Wenji said: What is the precedent?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Wenji had just been appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and was conducting affairs at the Censorate. Circuit memorial-presenting officials came to congratulate. Wenji asked: What is the precedent?

sentences.zh: 」臺吏喬德威等言：「朝廷在長安日，進奏官見大夫中丞，如胥吏見長官之禮。

translations.literal: Censorate clerks Qiao Dewei and others said: When the court was in Chang'an, memorial-presenting officials who met the Censor-in-Chief or Vice Censor-in-Chief observed the ritual of clerks meeting their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate clerks Qiao Dewei and others said: When the court was in Chang'an, memorial-presenting officials who met the Censor-in-Chief or Vice Censor-in-Chief observed the ritual of clerks meeting their superiors.

sentences.zh: 及梁氏將革命，本朝微弱，諸藩強據，人主大臣姑息邸吏，時中丞上事，邸吏雖至，皆於客次傳語，竟不相見。

translations.literal: When the House of Liang was about to seize power, our court was weak and the frontier commissions held sway; sovereign and ministers indulged the lodge clerks. When a Vice Censor-in-Chief took office, though lodge clerks came, they all conveyed messages in the reception room and never met face to face.
translations.idiomatic: When the House of Liang was about to seize power, the court was weak and frontier commissions held sway; sovereign and ministers indulged the lodge clerks. When a Vice Censor-in-Chief took office, though lodge clerks came, they all conveyed messages in the reception room and never met face to face.

sentences.zh: 自經兵亂，便以為常。

translations.literal: Since the military disorders, this has been taken as normal.
translations.idiomatic: Since the military disorders, this had been taken as normal.

sentences.zh: 」文紀令臺吏諭以舊儀相見，據案端簡，通名贊拜。

translations.literal: Wenji ordered the censorate clerks to instruct them in the old ritual of meeting face to face: seated upright at the desk with tablets in hand, announcing names and performing the bow of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji ordered the censorate clerks to instruct them in the old ritual of meeting face to face: seated upright at the desk with tablets in hand, announcing names and performing the bow of praise.

sentences.zh: 邸吏輩既出，怒不自勝，相率於閣門求見，騰口喧訴。

translations.literal: When the lodge clerks left, unable to contain their anger, they went in a body to the Gate Office to seek audience and clamored in loud complaint.
translations.idiomatic: When the lodge clerks left, unable to contain their anger, they went in a body to the Gate Office to seek audience and clamored in loud complaint.

sentences.zh: 明宗謂趙鳳曰：「進奏官比外何官？

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong said to Zhao Feng: Compared with outside offices, what rank are memorial-presenting officials?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong asked Zhao Feng: Compared with outside offices, what rank were memorial-presenting officials?

sentences.zh: 」鳳對曰：「府縣發遞祗候之流也。

translations.literal: Feng replied: They are of the sort who dispatch couriers and attend at prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Feng replied: They were of the sort who dispatch couriers and attend at prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「乃吏役耳，安得慢吾法官。

translations.literal: Mingzong said: They are mere clerical servants—how can they slight my law officers?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: They are mere clerical servants—how can they slight my law officers?

sentences.zh: 」乃下此詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon this edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon this edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年二月，以御史中丞為清望正四品。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, second month, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was made an esteemed clear office of the fourth rank, grade one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Tianfu (940), Jin made the Vice Censor-in-Chief an esteemed clear office at fourth rank, grade one.

sentences.zh: 按《唐典》，御史中丞正五品上，今始升之。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Regulations, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was fifth rank grade one upper; now he was raised for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Regulations the Vice Censor-in-Chief had been fifth rank, grade one upper; now he was raised for the first time.

sentences.zh: 三年三月壬戌，御史臺奏：「按《六典》，侍御史掌糾舉百僚，推鞫獄訟，居上者判臺，知公廨雜事，次和西推、贓贖、三司受事，次知東推、理匭。

translations.literal: On the day renxu of the third month of the third year, the Censorate memorialized: According to the Administrative Regulations, the Attending Censor supervises impeachment of the hundred officials and investigation of lawsuits; the senior one adjudicates the Censorate and manages miscellaneous bureau affairs; the next handles the Western Investigation, booty redemption, and cases received by the Three Offices; the next manages the Eastern Investigation and the complaint box.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu of the third month of the third year, the Censorate memorialized: Under the Administrative Regulations, the Attending Censor supervised impeachment of officials and investigation of lawsuits; the senior adjudicated the Censorate and managed bureau affairs; the next handled the Western Investigation, booty redemption, and cases received by the Three Offices; the next managed the Eastern Investigation and the complaint box.

sentences.zh: 」敕宜依舊制。

translations.literal: An edict said: The old regulations should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the old regulations be followed.

sentences.zh: 遂以駕部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事劉皞為河南少尹，自是無省郎知雜者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Hao, Vice Director of the Bureau of Equipage who concurrently served as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, was made Vice Governor of Henan; from then on no provincial bureau director served as miscellaneous-affairs censor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liu Hao, Vice Director of the Bureau of Equipage who concurrently served as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, was made Vice Governor of Henan; from then on no provincial bureau director served as miscellaneous-affairs censor.

sentences.zh: 開運二年八月，敕：「御史臺準前朝故事，以郎中、員外郎一人兼侍御史知雜事，近年停罷，獨委年深御史知雜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, eighth month, an edict said: The Censorate, following former-court precedent, had one Director or Vice Director concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; in recent years this was suspended, and only a senior censor was entrusted with miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Kaiyun (945), an edict said: The Censorate, following former-court precedent, had one Director or Vice Director concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; in recent years this had been suspended, and only a senior censor was entrusted with miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 振舉之間，紀綱未峻，宜遵舊事，庶葉通規。

translations.literal: In the effort to restore vigor, regulations have not been strict; the old practice should be followed, so that the general rules may be harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: In the effort to restore vigor, regulations had not been strict; the old practice should be followed so that the general rules might be harmonized.

sentences.zh: 宜卻於郎署中選清慎強幹者，兼侍御史知雜事。」

translations.literal: From the bureau directors one who is pure, cautious, and capable should again be chosen to serve concurrently as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs."
translations.idiomatic: From the bureau directors one who was pure, cautious, and capable should again be chosen to serve concurrently as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs."

sentences.zh: ──右御史臺

translations.literal: — The Censorate —
translations.idiomatic: — The Censorate —

sentences.zh: 後唐同光元年十月，崇政院依舊為樞密院，命宰臣郭崇韜兼樞密使，亦置直院一人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang of Later Tang, tenth month, the Court for Honoring Governance was restored as the Bureau of Military Affairs; the chief minister Guo Chongtao was ordered to serve concurrently as Commissioner of Military Affairs, and one duty officer of the bureau was also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Tongguang (923), Later Tang restored the Court for Honoring Governance as the Bureau of Military Affairs; chief minister Guo Chongtao was ordered to serve concurrently as Military Affairs Commissioner, and one duty officer was also appointed.

sentences.zh: 晉天福四年四月，以樞密副使張從恩為宣徽使，權廢樞密院故也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, fourth month, the Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Zhang Cong'en was made Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; this was because the Bureau of Military Affairs was provisionally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tianfu (939), Jin made Vice Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Cong'en Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat because the Bureau of Military Affairs had been provisionally abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉祖以宰臣桑維翰兼樞密使，懇求免職，只在中書，遂以宣徽使劉處讓代之，每有奏議，多不稱旨。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin founder had the chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Commissioner of Military Affairs; he earnestly sought to be relieved and remain only in the Secretariat, so the Palace Secretariat Commissioner Liu Churang replaced him; whenever he submitted proposals, they often failed to please.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jin founder had chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Military Affairs Commissioner; he earnestly sought relief to remain only in the Secretariat, so Palace Secretariat Commissioner Liu Churang replaced him; whenever he submitted proposals, they often failed to please.

sentences.zh: 其後處讓丁憂，乃以樞密印付中書門下，故有是厘改也。

translations.literal: Later Churang entered mourning, and the seal of Military Affairs was handed to the Secretariat and Chancellery; hence this reorganization.
translations.idiomatic: Later Churang entered mourning, and the Military Affairs seal was handed to the Secretariat and Chancellery; hence this reorganization.

sentences.zh: 開運元年六月，敕依舊置樞密院，以宰臣桑維翰兼樞密使，從中書門下奏請也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun, sixth month, an edict restored the Bureau of Military Affairs as before and had the chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Commissioner of Military Affairs, following a memorial from the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Kaiyun (944), an edict restored the Bureau of Military Affairs as before and had chief minister Sang Weihan serve concurrently as Military Affairs Commissioner, following a memorial from the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年六月，命司徒平章事範質、禮部尚書平章事王溥並參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande of Zhou, sixth month, Minister of Education Grand Councilor Fan Zhi and Minister of Rites Grand Councilor Wang Pu were both ordered to participate in the affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Xiande (959), Zhou ordered Minister of Education and Grand Councilor Fan Zhi and Minister of Rites and Grand Councilor Wang Pu both to participate in Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.

sentences.zh: 梁開平元年四月，始置建昌院，以博王友文判院事，以太祖在藩時，四鎮所管兵車賦稅、諸色課利，按舊簿籍而主之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, fourth month, the Jianchang Bureau was first established, with Prince of Bo Youwen as its director; it administered the troops, chariots, taxes, and various levies of the four commissions that the Founder had governed while in the frontier, according to the old registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Kaiping (907), Liang first established the Jianchang Bureau, with Prince of Bo Youwen as director; it administered the troops, chariots, taxes, and various levies of the four commissions the Founder had governed while in the frontier, according to the old registers.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，中書門下奏請以判建昌院事為建昌宮使，仍以東京太祖潛龍舊宅為宮也。

translations.literal: That year, fifth month, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized that the director of the Jianchang Bureau should be made Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace, and the Founder's former residence in the Eastern Capital where the hidden dragon had dwelt should serve as the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the fifth month, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized that the Jianchang Bureau director should become Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace, using the Founder's former Eastern Capital residence where the hidden dragon had dwelt as the palace.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，以侍中

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, the Palace Attendant
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, the Palace Attendant

sentences.zh: （案：原本有闕文，據《五代會要》，以侍中韓建判建昌宮事。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The original text is missing here. According to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, the Palace Attendant Han Jian was made director of Jianchang Palace affairs.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The original text is missing here. According to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, Palace Attendant Han Jian was made director of Jianchang Palace affairs.)]

sentences.zh: 判建昌宮事。

translations.literal: was made director of Jianchang Palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of Jianchang Palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 至十月，以尚書兵部侍郎李皎為建昌宮副使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Li Jiao, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Bureau of Personnel, was made Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Li Jiao, Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel in the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，以門下侍郎平章事薛貽矩兼延資庫使，判建昌宮事。

translations.literal: In the third year, ninth month, Xue Yiju, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was made concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and director of Jianchang Palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year, Xue Yiju, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was made concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and director of Jianchang Palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 至四年十二月，以李振為建昌宮副使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Li Zhen was made Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Li Zhen was made Vice Commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年五月，以門下侍郎平章事於兢兼延資庫使，判建昌宮事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianhua, fifth month, Yu Jing, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was made concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and director of Jianchang Palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Qianhua (912), Yu Jing, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, was made concurrent Commissioner of the Extended Resources Treasury and director of Jianchang Palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，廢建昌宮，以河南尹魏王張宗奭為國計使，凡天下金谷兵戎舊隸建昌宮者悉主之。

translations.literal: That year, sixth month, the Jianchang Palace was abolished; Zhang Zongshi, Prince of Wei and Governor of Henan, was made Commissioner of National Accounts, and all revenues, grain, and military affairs formerly under the Jianchang Palace were placed under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the sixth month, the Jianchang Palace was abolished; Zhang Zongshi, Prince of Wei and Governor of Henan, was made Commissioner of National Accounts, and all revenues, grain, and military affairs formerly under the Jianchang Palace were placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 至後唐同光四年二月，以吏部尚書李琪為國計使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang of Later Tang, second month, Li Qi, Minister of the Bureau of Personnel, was made Commissioner of National Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year of Tongguang (926), Later Tang made Li Qi, Minister of the Bureau of Personnel, Commissioner of National Accounts.

sentences.zh: 自後廢其名額不置。

translations.literal: Thereafter its title was abolished and the office was not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter its title was abolished and the office was not re-established.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光元年十一月，以左監門衛將軍、判內侍省李紹宏兼內勾，凡天下錢谷簿書，悉委裁遣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang of Later Tang, eleventh month, Li Shaohong, General of the Left Gate Guards and acting director of the Palace Domestic Service, was made concurrent Internal Auditor; all revenue registers of the realm were entrusted to his judgment and disposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tongguang (923), Later Tang made Li Shaohong, General of the Left Gate Guards and acting director of the Palace Domestic Service, concurrent Internal Auditor; all revenue registers of the realm were entrusted to his judgment and disposal.

sentences.zh: 自是州縣供帳繁費，議者非之。

translations.literal: From then on the provisioning accounts of prefectures and counties became lavish and costly; commentators criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the provisioning accounts of prefectures and counties became lavish and costly; commentators criticized this.

sentences.zh: 又內勾之名，人以為不祥之言。

translations.literal: Moreover, the name "Internal Auditor" was regarded by people as an inauspicious expression.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the title Internal Auditor was regarded as an inauspicious expression.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，敕鹽鐵、度支、戶部三司，凡關錢物，並委租庸使管轄，踵梁之舊制也。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, an edict placed the three offices of Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Census: all matters concerning money and goods were entrusted to the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée, following Liang's old system.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year (925), an edict placed the three offices of Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Census: all matters concerning money and goods were entrusted to the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée, following Liang's old system.

sentences.zh: 天成元年四月，詔廢租庸院，依舊為鹽鐵、戶部、度支三司，委宰臣一人專判。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, fourth month, an edict abolished the Tax and Corvée Bureau and restored the three offices of Salt and Iron, Census, and Revenue as before, with one chief minister exclusively adjudicating them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Tiancheng (926), an edict abolished the Tax and Corvée Bureau and restored the three offices of Salt and Iron, Census, and Revenue as before, with one chief minister exclusively adjudicating them.

sentences.zh: 長興元年八月，以許州節度張延朗行工部尚書，充三司使，班在宣徽使之下。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, eighth month, Zhang Yanlang, military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, was made Acting Minister of the Bureau of Works and Commissioner of the Three Offices, ranking below the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Changxing (930), Zhang Yanlang, military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, was made Acting Minister of the Bureau of Works and Commissioner of the Three Offices, ranking below the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三司置使，自延朗始也。

translations.literal: The establishment of a commissioner for the Three Offices began with Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: The establishment of a commissioner for the Three Offices began with Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 唐朝已來，戶部、度支掌泉貨，鹽鐵時置使名，戶部、度支則尚書省本司郎中、侍郎判其事。

translations.literal: Since the Tang dynasty, the Census and Revenue offices managed currency and goods; the Salt and Iron office sometimes had a commissioner by title, while the Census and Revenue offices were adjudicated by the directors and vice directors of their bureaus within the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tang dynasty, the Census and Revenue offices had managed currency and goods; the Salt and Iron office sometimes had a commissioner by title, while the Census and Revenue offices were adjudicated by the directors and vice directors of their bureaus within the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，楊慎矜、王鉷、楊國忠繼以聚貨之術，媚上受寵，然皆守戶部、度支本官，別帶使額，亦無所改作。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong in succession used methods of amassing goods to flatter the sovereign and win favor; yet all retained their original posts in the Census and Revenue offices, bearing commissioner titles separately, and made no changes to the system.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong in succession used methods of amassing revenue to flatter the sovereign and win favor; yet all retained their original posts in the Census and Revenue offices, bearing commissioner titles separately, and made no changes to the system.

sentences.zh: 下及劉晏、第五琦亦如舊制。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yan and Diwu Qi also followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yan and Diwu Qi also followed the old system.

sentences.zh: 自後亦以宰臣各判一司，不置使額。

translations.literal: Thereafter chief ministers also adjudicated one office each, and no commissioner title was established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter chief ministers also adjudicated one office each, and no commissioner title was established.

sentences.zh: 乾符後，天下兵興，隨處置租庸使以主調發，兵罷則停。

translations.literal: After Qianfu, warfare arose throughout the realm; wherever needed a Commissioner of Tax and Corvée was appointed to manage mobilization, and when the troops were dismissed the post ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianfu, warfare arose throughout the realm; wherever needed a Commissioner of Tax and Corvée was appointed to manage mobilization, and when troops were dismissed the post ceased.

sentences.zh: 梁時乃置租庸使，專天下泉貨。

translations.literal: In the Liang period the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée was then established, monopolizing the realm's currency and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée was then established, monopolizing the realm's currency and goods.

sentences.zh: 莊宗中興，秉政者不閑典故，踵梁朝故事，復置租庸使，以魏博故吏孔謙專使務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong restored the dynasty, those in power were unversed in precedent and followed Liang's example, restoring the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée and entrusting the former Wei-Bo clerk Kong Qian exclusively with its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong restored the dynasty, those in power were unversed in precedent and followed Liang's example, restoring the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée and entrusting the former Wei-Bo clerk Kong Qian exclusively with its affairs.

sentences.zh: 斂怨於天下，斫喪王室者，實租庸之弊故也。

translations.literal: The gathering of resentment throughout the realm and the cutting down of the royal house were in truth due to the abuses of the Tax and Corvée system.
translations.idiomatic: The gathering of resentment throughout the realm and the cutting down of the royal house were in truth due to the abuses of the Tax and Corvée system.

sentences.zh: 洎明宗嗣位，思革其弊，未及下車，乃詔削除使名，但命重臣一人判其事，曰判三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, he wished to reform its abuses; before he had even taken office, he issued an edict abolishing the commissioner title and ordering only one senior minister to adjudicate the affairs, called Adjudicator of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, he wished to reform its abuses; before he had even taken office, he issued an edict abolishing the commissioner title and ordering only one senior minister to adjudicate the affairs, called Adjudicator of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 至是，延朗自許州入再掌國計，白於樞密使，請置三司名。

translations.literal: At this time Yanlang entered from Xu Prefecture to take charge of national accounts again; he informed the Military Affairs Commissioner and requested that the title of the Three Offices be established.

translations.idiomatic: In recent times, when civil officials' ranks rose slightly, they were granted Pillar of the State, and before much time passed were transferred to Supreme Pillar of the State;

translations.literal: for military qualifications, regardless of who, upon first appointment they were granted Supreme Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: for military qualifications, regardless of who, upon first appointment they were granted Supreme Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 官爵非無次第，階勛備有等差，宜自此時，重修舊制。

translations.literal: Offices and noble ranks are not without order; ranks and merit have their gradations. From this time the old system should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Offices and noble ranks are not without order; ranks and merit have their gradations. From this time the old system should be restored.

translations.literal: Henceforth, whenever merit is added, one must begin with Cavalry Captain, pass through twelve promotions before receiving Supreme Pillar of the State, and this shall forever be the rule, not to be exceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever merit was added, one must begin with Cavalry Captain, pass through twelve promotions before receiving Supreme Pillar of the State, and this was to remain the rule, not to be exceeded.

translations.idiomatic: Western Han used the six criteria of the inspector to examine prefects and governors; the five bureaus of the Department of State Affairs summarized all achievements—the law was especially precise, and officials were held to account.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei provisionally established grades in the army, debated the purity or corruption of officials, and appointed men according to clerical rank, abruptly departing from former rules.

translations.literal: Since Sui and Tang it was first written into statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sui and Tang it was first written into statutes.

sentences.zh: 應順元年春三月戊午，宗正上言：「故事，諸陵有令、丞各一員，近令、丞不俱置，便委本縣令兼之。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu in the third month of spring in the first year of Yingshun, the Directorate of the Imperial Clan submitted a memorial: "By precedent, each imperial tomb had one Director and one Vice Director; recently Director and Vice Director have not both been appointed, and the local county magistrate has been entrusted to serve concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu in the third month of spring in the first year of Yingshun (960), the Directorate of the Imperial Clan memorialized: "By precedent, each imperial tomb had one Director and one Vice Director; recently Director and Vice Director had not both been appointed, and the local county magistrate had been entrusted to serve concurrently.

sentences.zh: 緣河南、洛陽是京邑，恐兼令、丞不便。

translations.literal: Because Henan and Luoyang are the capital region, we fear that concurrent service as Director and Vice Director would be inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Because Henan and Luoyang were the capital region, they feared that concurrent service as Director and Vice Director would be inconvenient."
